taxonomyNote: NatureServe's primary name is Red River Mudpuppy; some authorities treat it as a subspecies of N. maculosus, and NatureServe says its status needs further research.
fieldMarks: Smaller than the mudpuppy, maximum about 12 inches; lighter grey-brown or red-brown ground colour.
Dark spots on the upper body more distinct and more numerous than on the mudpuppy.
Belly has a wide, light, unspotted central area, light grey with pale pink edges.
habitat: Missouri's mudpuppy account says mudpuppies are permanently aquatic in large creeks, rivers and reservoirs, hiding by day under logs, rocks and debris; the Red River mudpuppy replaces the common mudpuppy in the southernmost quarter of the state.
range: Northern Louisiana north to Arkansas, eastern Oklahoma, southern Missouri and southeastern Kansas.

lookalikes.name: Mudpuppy
lookalikes.howToTell: Common mudpuppy is larger (to about 19 in); Red River mudpuppy has a lighter ground colour, more numerous spots and a wide pale unspotted belly strip.
